text: Started a new city, Claudeville, on Easy ($20,000) in the year 2000. Turned off disasters, Extra!!! newspapers, and auto-goto so the camera stays put.
Placed a gas power plant ($2,000, 50 MW): cheaper than coal and cleaner, enough power for the first ~5,000 people.
Built the main road heading northwest through the big flat plain, avoiding the small pond next to the plant.
Zoned light residential at the far (northwest) end, light commercial in the middle, and light industry next to the power plant, so factory pollution stays away from homes.
Nothing grew for 5 years. Found the power line stopped one tile short of the plant (fixed), then lined every zone with power lines and added a water pump with pipes under all zones.

Restarting the city. After 7 game years nothing grew: my first layout had broken power links and power lines between the zones and the road. Starting over with a simpler, tighter layout so the 30-year clock restarts cleanly.
New flat map made in the map editor. Claudeville refounded Jan 2000 with $20,000, disasters off.
Gas power plant at the east end of a 40-tile main road along the flat northern plain. Side road north toward the map edge for future neighbor links.
Zones now touch the road directly: light industry next to the plant, commercial in the middle, residential at the far west end. Power lines run along the outer edge of every zone strip.
First buildings under construction by April 2000. The new layout works.
Added a coal power plant (200 MW) after a 'power plant needed' warning; the gas plant was maxed out.
Added a water pump and pipes under the power lines so buildings can grow denser.
Unemployment hit 35%, so zoned a new industrial strip on a second road (y=19) to create jobs. Commercial demand is negative, so no new shops yet.
Jan 2009, pop 2,110: unemployment fell to 13% and housing demand turned positive, so I added a new road along the north and zoned 87 tiles of light residential there, away from the factories.
Jan 2012, pop 3,220: factory demand is maxed and unemployment is 9%. Zoned ~80 more industrial tiles south of the bottom road, with two short power lines into them.

Found that only 15 of ~390 buildings had water: one pump on dry land was far too small, and buildings were being abandoned. Added 8 pumps along the river bank by the power plants, with pipes into the network and into the southern factories.
Built the first police station ($500) in the middle of town; crime was rising with no police at 3,000 people.
Added 5 more water pumps along the river bank (13 total); the southern factories and western homes were dry and being abandoned.

Built a road to the north map edge, which made a trade connection with the neighbor city Villa (about $1,000). Abandoned factories had power, water, no crime and low pollution, so I suspect they lacked trade routes.

Diagnosed the stall: main roads were at maximum traffic, so trips failed and buildings were abandoned. Turned the two long power-line rows (y=7 and y=15) into roads, doubling the east-west routes, and kept power flowing with line crossings.
Southern factory block was cut off (road links only at its far ends) and its west half had no power. Added two short connector roads and a power crossing.
Cut property tax from 7% to 5% to boost growth; 5 years left to reach 5,000. Tax income is only ~$300/yr, and the $9k cash buffer covers it.
Zoned dense residential in the empty block east of the central road (rows 16-18), with a power crossing.
Jan 2027, pop 3,800: housing demand is maxed and unemployment fell to 11% after the tax cut. Zoned dense residential along the north edge, above the top road.
Final push for 5,000 by 2030 (pop 4,240 in Jan 2029): laid water pipes to the new north and east housing and added 12 more pumps (26 total).
Cut property tax to 3% for the final growth year. I'll raise it again for the 3 profitable years.

Missed goal 1: population was 4,410 in Jan 2030, short of 5,000 by the 30-year deadline. Growth stalled for years (2013-2024) from water shortages and traffic jams before I found the causes. Population is 4,610 in Jan 2031.
